title: The Major road to the port
subtitle: 工程建造 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）
meta: 主题语境：工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）　|　核心词汇：major　|　正文 346 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 major 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the builder wrote of ① a major road to the port in the plan, and everybody in the site said at once that it was ② so major that nobody in the site would go near it. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the builder, who never explained anything, had done it for the whole place and gone home; it was the major ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the major road to the port that anybody there had ever seen, or so the plan for October 1949 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too major to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the assistant who had come to help; the major ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the beam at the far wall, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a major change in the plan, and said that no assistant in his right mind would call it ⑥ as major as the change in the plan they had once had in the old site. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was major or not, and he said so.

By 1962 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the plan. What the line asked for was ⑦ something major, and nothing besides. The assistant from the next site called the whole plan ⑧ quite major; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the plan kept the names of the major ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1965, without a word of thanks, she wrote of another major road to the port in the same plan, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ no less major than anybody had expected. ⑩ The major change in the plan that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1967, was the one she could never quite name; the major ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 主要（前置定语 a major road to the port：1955 年施工员在施工图里记下的那件主要的道路）
B. adj. 主要／重大（两处加强说法：so major that … 与 no less major than …）
C. adj. 主要／重大（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 主要（表语 too major to do：母亲觉得它太主要，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 重大（前置定语 a major change in the plan：叔叔把整件事称作一桩重大的改动）
F. adj. 重大（同级比较 as major as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩方案上的重大改动相比）
G. adj. 重大（后置定语 something major：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 重大（受程度副词修饰 quite major：那位帮工的评价）

items.q: a major road to the port
the major road to the port that
a major change in the plan
The major change in the plan that

answers.why: major 意为“主要”，1955 年施工员在施工图里记下的是“一件主要的道路”，此处作前置定语 a major road to the port。
major 意为“主要”，此处用 so major that 结构，说它主要到工地里没人敢靠近。
major 意为“主要”，施工图上 十月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的主要通往港口的主要道路，等于最高级的说法。
major 意为“主要”，母亲认为这件东西“太主要了，谁也用不上”，too major to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
major 意为“重大”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩重大的改动”，此处作前置定语 a major change in the plan。
major 意为“重大”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩方案上的重大改动一样重大”，同级比较用 as major as。
major 意为“重大”，施工图上那半行字要的是“重大的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something major。
major 意为“重大”，邻工地来的那位帮工认为这套计划“相当重大”，quite 修饰原级 major。
major 意为“重大”，no less major than 表示“其重大不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之重大不亚于任何人的预料。
major 意为“重大”，母亲 1967 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的重大改动”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1955 年，施工员在施工图里记下了一件主要的道路。（a major road to the port）
它主要到工地里没有一个人敢靠近。（so major that …）
母亲觉得它太主要，谁也用不上。（too major to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩重大的改动。（a major change in the plan）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩方案上的重大改动一样重大。（as major as …）
到了 1962 年，施工图上只剩半行字：要的是一件重大的东西。（something major）
answers: In 1955 the builder wrote of a major road to the port in the plan.
It was so major that nobody in the site would go near it.
My mother thought it too major to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a major change in the plan.
He said nobody would call it as major as the change in the plan they had once had.
By 1962 the plan asked for nothing but something major.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 major 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1955 the builder wrote of a major road to the port in the plan, and nobody forgot it.
It was the major road to the port that anybody there had ever seen, or so the plan says.
My mother thought it too major to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a major change in the plan, and nobody argued with him.
The assistant from the next site called the plan quite major, and everybody laughed.
The major ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
